The instant one is the second petition fil filed by the petitioner under Section 483 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short "BNSS")) for grant of regular bail in case arising out of FIR No. No.0035 0035 dated 13.08.2024 registered under Section 66D of Information Information Technology Act and Section 420 of IPC (Section 467, 468, 471, 201, 204, 120B of IPC added later on) at Police Station Cyber Crime, District Rewari.

sentences.text: After registration of FIR, investigation proceedings were initiated.
It was revealed that Consumer Consumer Application Form (CAF) of one of the mobile number used for making calls to the complainant pertained to the present petitioner.
He was arrested on 09.01.2025.
Recovery of an amount of Rs.6 lakhs, out of the duped amount was got effected from him.
Investigation now stands completed.
mpleted.

4. The previous petition as filed by the petitioner had been dismissed by this Court by making the following observations ::-
The petitioner in connivance with the co co-accused, accused, is alleged to have defrauded and cheated the complainant by making ca calls lls and sending emails.
The last IP address of WhatsApp which was used for cheating the complainant was found to be in the name of the petitioner.
The petitioner was occupying the off officee at the address where this WiFi connection was taken.
Though he took a plea that he had demitted those premises long back, but there is nothing on the record to show so.
The allegations against the petitioner are grave in nature.
Crimes of this nature are on the rise and have 2 of 5 becoming a growing menace in today's digital age.
Cyber criminals are using sophisticated methods to target public persons and institutions.
A stringed approach to deter offenders is required.
The gamut of above discussed circumstances does not call for grant of benefit of bail to the petitioner.

Accordingly,
the petition does not deserve to be allowed and is dismissed.
5.
It is argued by learned counsel for the petitioner that after the dismissal of his previous petition, a period of almost six months has elapsed.
However, there has not been much much progress in the trial as only 02 out of 17 prosecution witnesses have been examined so far.
The trial will take considerable time to conclude.
The complainant has entered into a compromise with him and he has no objection if the petition is allowed.
Even otherwise, no useful purpose is going to be served by detaining him in custody anymore.
Each day spent by him in custody has furnished him a new ground to seek concession of bail.
It is thus, argued that the petition deserves to be allowed.
6. Per contra, learned State counsel while relying upon the status report has argued that the allegations against the petitioner are quite serious in nature.
His previous petition had been dismissed by passing a detailed order.
There is no drastic or substantive substantive change in the circumstances.
There is no material on record to show that the complainant has entered into any compromise with the petitioner.

Even if it is so, still the petitioner has committed a crime against the society also as the allegations show that he was 3 of 5 an active participant in the commission of offence of cyber crime as against the complainant.
It is, therefore, argued that the petition is not maintainable and is liable to be dismissed.

sentences.text: This Court has heard the rival submissions made by learned counsel for the parties at considerable length.

8. Undoubtedly, a second/successive petition is maintainable in law, however, for such a period petition to succeed, the petitioner must show some substantial change in the circumstances and showing of a mere superficial or ostensible change would not suffice.

Reference in this regard can be drawn to the observations made by this Court in CRA-S-2322 2322-2022 titled as Rafiq Khan Versus State of Haryana and another, wherein it was observed so and it was further urther held that in case a Court chooses to grant second/successive regular bail petition, cogent and lucid reasons are pertinently required to be recorded for granting such plea.

entities.text: Rafiq Khan Versus State of Haryana and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the instant case, the only ground which is taken by the petitioner is prolonged olonged period of incarceration.
However, the petitioner has been booked for and is facing trial for commission of serious offences.

He had not only prepared and sent fake receipts to the complainant to convince him that insurance policies were issued in in his favour but also used his WiFi ID for the purpose of making calls by impersonating himself himself, for sending e-mails mails and fraudulent and fabricated documents to the complainant.
He is a habitual offender as one more case of similar nature is pending agains againstt him.
Merely because he has spent more time in custody, custody cannot be considered to be a reason 4 of 5 for extending benefit of bail to him.

Taking into consideration the above discussed facts, this Court is of the considered opinion that there is no substantive orr drastic change in the circumstances on the basis of which the petitioner should be extended benefit of bail and hence no ground has been made for allowing the petition.
Accordingly, the same is dismissed.

9. It is, however, clarified that the observati observations ons made above shall not be construed as an expression of opinion of this Court on the merits of the case and shall not influence the outcome of the trial in any manner.
10. Since the main petition has been dismissed pending application, if any, is rendered infructuous.
